findings.title: Concurrent callers can build and publish different indexes for the same key
findings.body: The cache is now locked only when assigning `b.cache[key]`, so two callers can both observe a missing index in `GetIndex` and execute the full `BuildIndex` concurrently for the same NamespacedResource. For file-backed indexes, the second `bleve.New` attempts to create the same directory and fails, causing otherwise valid searches or watch-event indexing to fail. For memory indexes, whichever build finishes last replaces the cache with its snapshot; that snapshot can predate writes indexed by the other build, making recently written documents disappear from the active index. Coordinate cache lookup and creation per key (for example, with keyed singleflight) while allowing distinct keys to build concurrently.

findings.title: Eager startup makes normal shutdown able to panic on a closed watch channel
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now always calls `Init`, which starts this watcher even if the server never handles an RPC. When the SQL backend is stopped, its poller closes the event stream; receiving from that closed channel yields a nil `*WrittenEvent`, and the immediately following accesses to `v.Type` and `v.Key` panic. The equivalent unchecked receive in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` line 209 has the same problem for the search watcher. Receive with `v, ok := <-events` and exit when `ok` is false (and ensure the goroutines observe cancellation) so an idle server can start and stop safely.

findings.title: Constructor failures leave initialized background services running
findings.body: If `s.search.init` succeeds but `s.initWatcher` subsequently fails, this path returns `nil, err` without cancelling `s.ctx` or stopping the lifecycle hooks. `search.init` has already started a watch loop using `context.Background()`, so the discarded server can continue polling the backend indefinitely; the successfully initialized lifecycle resources are also never stopped. This is newly reachable because initialization now occurs inside the constructor and the caller receives no server instance on which to call `Stop`. Clean up/cancel initialized components before returning a constructor error, and do not use an uncancellable background context for the search watcher.
